q1.note: The people-in-frame count is 5 from 10:01:01 to 10:02:41. The count-per-second data is the most reliable source (about ±1).

q2.note: The count never went above 5. It also reached 5 in four other periods: 10:04:50–10:04:55, 10:05:03–10:05:37 and 10:06:20–10:07:56.

q3.note: The Op 16 zone is empty from 10:08:06 to 10:09:18. In the same period Op 17 shows 2 persons, so the Op 16 operator seems to have stood at Op 17 and returned at 10:09:18.

q4.note: No other empty period for Op 14 to Op 17 lasted longer than about 12 s. These periods come straight from the zone counts, so they are fairly reliable.

q6.note: The 10:01 Op 14 worker left the view at the east edge at 10:02:41. The person who took Op 14 at 10:04:25 appeared when the tracks were confused at Bench L, and could be the former Op 15 worker or the person who entered at 10:03:48 (possibly the same person returning), so who it is cannot be established.

q7.note: Op 14 is empty from 10:01:42 to 10:04:25 in the zone counts.

q8.note: One continuous track follows this path and left the view at 10:02:41. The Op 16 operator also left that zone at about 10:01:57, and a track from Bench R left at the east edge at 10:03:17, but that track is broken and cannot be linked to the Op 16 operator.

q9.note: There were 4 people in view at the start, and 4 entries followed. Some entries may be people coming back after they left: 10:06:20 likely matches the 10:05:37 exit and 10:03:48 likely matches an earlier exit, so 6 is the best guess. The very short ghost tracks (E, G, H, J, L, M) do not change the counts, so they are not counted as people.
